verdict.printed: Page 272 (De inventione I, f. 106): the end of the eighth topic of indignation (crimes against those one was raised and taught by, the dead, the wretched, boys, the old, women), then topics nine through fourteen, breaking off at the start of the fifteenth ('inimicis quoque et hosti-').
verdict.evidence: The English covers all of page 272, from 'against those by whom you were raised' to 'even enemies and foes'. It then goes on to translate all of page 273: 'Complaint is a speech capturing the pity of the auditors... The sixth is that through which it is shown that one is in misery beyond expectation... but', which is printed on page 273.

verdict.printed: Page 323: the end of the answer about the Fall ('worden. Das ware die Folge des Falls...'), Question 33 'Bliebe er im Gehorsam?' with its answer, and Anmerckungen note 1 up to 'in der sinnebildischen Spra-'
verdict.evidence: Page 343 is rendered in full ('33. Did he remain in obedience?' through 'in the symbolic language'). After that the English goes on with all of page 344 ('of the Holy Spirit, belongs in another investigation... 2. I would wish that the Author...' up to 'could not withdraw') and then with text from a later page that is not on any of the three pages ('from Himself and over which He had to be jealous... 34. What was his sin then?...').

verdict.printed: Page 387 (קפה): the end of the lead-in to the Priestly Blessing ('by the hand of Moses Your servant...'), the three verses with direction notes (towards the sanctuary, right, left), the congregation's responses with acronyms (אנקת"ם, פסת"ם, etc.), and 'Adir ba-marom', followed by the Etz Yosef, Dover Shalom, Acharit le-Shalom and Iyun Tefillah commentaries
verdict.evidence: The English matches page 387: 'by the hand of Moses, Your servant... Aaron and his sons, the priests', the verses 'May the Lord bless you and protect you', the margin acronyms 'A.N.K.T.M.' and 'Mighty in the heights, dwelling in power' are all printed on page 387. But the Dover Shalom rendering is mostly made-up words in brackets and doesn't follow the print. The Acharit le-Shalom column is left out, and Iyun Tefillah stops after its first line.

verdict.printed: A page of Zohar Aramaic in Sephardic cursive, with a main block, a right-hand margin column and a lower block. It is a dialogue among Rabbi Yehudah, Rabbi Shimon, Rabbi Elazar, Rabbi Abba and Rabbi Yitzhak, continuing the Zohar text from page 697.
verdict.evidence: "Through this, the opinion of Maimonides... in The Guide for the Perplexed (Part II, Chapter 2) is reconciled" and "Necessary Existent... Intellect, the Intelligible, and the Intelligent" are not on page 698, 697 or 699. The scans show Zohar dialogue among rabbis, not a philosophical treatise about Maimonides, Ibn Ezra, Abarbanel or Alshich. The English translates a made-up transcription, not the printed page.

verdict.printed: Page 254 (LIBER II., fol. 125): De divinatione II, from 'et hostem, et hospitem uidit' (Deiotarus and Caesar) through the lituus of Romulus, the whetstone of Attius Navius and the origins of augury, to 'plerique etiam summum bonum dicunt. num'
verdict.evidence: Page 254 is fully rendered, from 'and he saw both his enemy and his guest' to 'Most even call it the supreme good.' The English then carries on with all of page 255: 'Does the frequency of their opinion deter the Stoics…', the Ennius and Ajax verses, and Aemilia, Paulus and Caecilia. It ends with an invented sentence printed on none of the three pages: 'will that matter bring you fear or excitement?'

verdict.printed: Page 124 (printed 125): from '— теперь такъ» — ни мольбы, ни увѣщанія не помогутъ' (Ivan Ilyich cast out of the common world, the long quoted court scene, 'неужели только она правда?', the cobra-and-bird image) through '…смотрѣлъ на нее и, ничего не дѣлая, невыра-'
verdict.evidence: The English begins with all of page 123 (printed 124): 'self-willed daring provokes indignation… Aristotle opposed the peculiar worlds of dreamers… play whist, talk about politics'. It then renders all of page 124 ('neither pleas nor exhortations will help… unspeakably suffer'). It ends with the opening of page 125 (printed 126): 'Or as Tolstoy describes a bit later: … he would go into his study, lie down, and remain alone with her. Face to face with her…'

verdict.printed: Page 295: 'Fig. 299', a colour plate of Lou-pan with the characters 魯班 in the upper right, and the caption 'Lou-pan, patron des menuisiers. Intendant du ministère des Travaux publics du ciel.'
verdict.evidence: 'Lu Ban, patron of carpenters. Superintendent of the Ministry of Public Works of Heaven.' renders the caption printed on page 295. The added note 'Lu Ban, who lived from approximately 507 to 444 BC, was a famous Chinese engineer...' is outside background that is not printed on any of the three pages. The meta line about a 'previous illustration of the Cowherd and the Weaver Girl' is also not on any of these pages.

verdict.printed: Page 477: a handwritten Sanskrit worked calculation with number strings for Venus (śukra), the Sun (ravi), vitribha-lagna, śara, nati, sthityardha, dṛgāsava, cara and yugānāsava, with an eGangotri stamp at the bottom
verdict.evidence: '3388 Venus 3332 ... having multiplied 5230' and the closing 'Venus 13 21 15 in the calculation 22 22 visible...' follow the first and last lines of page 477 (३३८८ शुक्रः ... / ...शुक्रः १३२१ १५ लेवने २२२२ दृष्टा). The only additions are short term glosses and the meta/summary lines.

verdict.printed: Page 630 (numbered 553): the heading 'Absinthium alpinum.' above a full-page woodcut of the plant, showing its roots, divided leaves and a cluster of flowers at the top.
verdict.evidence: '# Alpine wormwood' translates the heading 'Absinthium alpinum.' printed on page 630. The rest is a short description of that page's woodcut (roots, divided leaves, flower cluster), and nothing in it comes from pages 629 or 631.

verdict.printed: A full-page woodcut of Christ washing the disciples' feet inside an ornamental border, with a small triangular mark at the lower left and no text.
verdict.evidence: The English body, 'Jesus Christ, identifiable by his halo, is kneeling on the right... washing the feet of a disciple', describes the picture on page 357. The added parts are minor: a gloss of 'Mandatum' as Latin for 'command' and a meta line tying the image to the humility chapter on page 356.

verdict.printed: Page 10 shows the second half of the Imperial Academy (太學圖) woodblock plan: rows of halls labelled 廣業堂, 崇志堂, 正義堂, 誠心堂, 修道堂, 率性堂 and 彝倫堂, with a gate complex at the bottom.
verdict.evidence: 'Hall of Broad Achievement' (廣業堂) through 'Hall of Moral Relations' (彝倫堂) are the hall labels printed on page 10. The notes on the student-progression system and the Emperor's lectures are background not printed on any page, but they are presented as notes and meta-commentary, not as the page's text.

verdict.printed: Page 336 (CAP. III): the end of Pragmatia III (the temple doors closing, the dancing figures, a reference to Hero's Automata), then Pragmatia IV on turning wheels that pour lustral water, with Clement and Hero quoted, an engraving of the cylindrical vessel and a margin note
verdict.evidence: 'Some desire that, with the door open, various monsters of the gods...' and 'Clement of Alexandria says in Stromata, Book 6' are printed on page 338. The English leaves out the page's first lines ('connectebantur, aperiuntur; situlâ verò humore repletâ ... mysteriosâ quâdam operatione peragebatur'). It also shortens the last line, dropping 'inferius H L, diaphragmate H B discriminatum; habeat autem vas A B in fundo'. The only addition is the gloss 'ritual purification'.

verdict.printed: Page 13: woodblock frontal-view acupoint chart of a child figure titled 正面圖, with point labels such as 百會, 天突, 中脘, 期門, 天樞, 曲池, 三里, 風市, 三陰交, 內庭, 行間 and 大敦.
verdict.evidence: 'Frontal View Diagram' and the point names 'Hundred Convergences (百會)', 'Celestial Chimney (天突)' and 'Great Mound (大敦)' render the title and labels printed on page 13. The added material is not printed on any of the three pages: the meta note on the move from safety rules to a practical guide, the term glosses for the Conception Vessel and acupuncture, and the sentence 'These represent the primary acupuncture points... to balance the body's vital energy'.

verdict.printed: Page 131 (headed 'Tertium') carries on the commentary on lunar eclipses: shadow vs. darkness, Almias's eclipse explained by refraction, the four kinds of lunar eclipse with a lettered shadow/moon diagram (a–l), then the start of the commentary on 'Cum autem fuerit luna' (solar eclipse).
verdict.evidence: 'as Almias says in his De Mundi Mirabilibus, a lunar eclipse was seen with both luminaries appearing' and 'let us describe the earth's shadow a b c d opposite the sun, the diameter of which is f g' are both printed on page 131. The added notes are short glosses, e.g. 'likely a reference to Al-Māhānī'. The English stops at 'Then, when he says, "But when the moon', so the last ~5 lines of page 131 (on the cause of solar eclipse) are not rendered.

verdict.printed: Page 65: the second half of the sutra (śeṣārgha-guṇaka-yoga minus one gives the purchase price), followed by the continuation of the upapatti derivation, showing that the profit (vi·śe−1)/sa is the same for everyone and that vi must be chosen so this comes out as a whole number
verdict.evidence: 'This measure of profit is the same everywhere' renders 'इदं लाभमानं सर्वत्र समानमेव', printed on page 102. The additions are a meta note, a summary, short glosses and a vocabulary note on 'yāvat-tāvat', a term not printed on the page. The page number is given as 45 but the scan reads ६५ (65).

verdict.printed: Nothing: page 4 is a blank leaf showing only paper texture and fibres, with marbled board edges visible.
verdict.evidence: 'This page serves as a flyleaf or endpaper... used to protect the decorative frontispiece' is commentary written for the page and is not printed on any page. The meta's 'symbolic frontispiece featuring the Rose Cross and the Pelican' does not appear on pages 3, 4 or 5, which are all blank.

verdict.printed: Page 18: running head 'INTRODVCTIO IN' over a woodcut of a right palm with six labels: Linea mesal. fortune, Linea vite uel cord., Linea media nat., L. epatis fo., Percussio man., Restricta mulieris
verdict.evidence: 'The line of life, or of the heart' renders the label 'Linea vite, uel cord.' printed on the hand on page 18. The added notes on each line (for example, that it is 'known today as the Head Line') are short glosses, so the additions count as minor.

verdict.printed: Faint, non-mirrored text: the end of a list of booksellers/places, a line 'Mais aussi apud ... reperiuntur' (roughly), the French notice 'AVIS AU RELIEUR' with a short paragraph about figures and vignettes, and the same notice in Dutch, 'BERICHT AAN DEN BOEKBINDER'
verdict.evidence: '->NOTICE TO THE READER.<-' and 'a certain number of figures... vignettes' loosely render the faint French 'AVIS AU RELIEUR' paragraph printed on page 938, though the heading actually means 'notice to the binder'. The bookseller list and the Dutch notice are reduced to '...' or left out, and the meta's claim that this is a '1724 edition of Christiaan Huygens' collected works' is added background that is not on the page.

verdict.printed: Page 462: the end of the Sanskrit commentary on how to find the bhuja (north-south distance) and the sphuta-bhuja of the Sun and Moon, with the 140/90/50 kala example, then the Hindi भाषाभाष्य and the start of the उपपत्ति
verdict.evidence: 'Suppose the Moon's side is 140 north. The Sun's side is 90 Kalas north... leaves a true side of 50' renders चन्द्रस्योत्तरो भुजः ... १४० ... नवतिः ९० ... ५० on page 546. The only additions are the short meta/summary framing and the term glosses.

verdict.printed: Page 93 is a blank endpaper. The only thing on it is a Getty Center Library barcode sticker reading '3 3125 00113 4143'.
verdict.evidence: 'The Lantern must be proportioned to the mass of the dome...' and the whole text on dome construction, including the materials table, does not appear on page 93, 92 or 94. All three are blank endpapers or covers, so the English was made up, and it leaves out the barcode label.

verdict.printed: Red cloth book cover with a torn, bordered paper label reading 'बृहत्पाराशरहोरा-शास्त्रम् ।' and the CC-0 Shri Krishna Museum, Kurukshetra / eGangotri watermark. All three scans show this same cover.
verdict.evidence: 'THE GREAT PARASHARA ASTROLOGY- TREATISE.' translates the label title printed on page -1695. The additions are background glosses that appear on no page: the note's word-by-word breakdown, the Technical Vocabulary entries (Parashara–Maitreya dialogue, Jyotisha as a Vedanga), the guessed '19th or early 20th-century' date and the bridging meta sentence 'Following the initial assessment...'.

verdict.printed: Page 378: the Argumentum to Fam. IX.6, the full letter of Cicero to Varro (Caninius noster ... Vale), and the start of its Explanatio (Adventus ... Alsiense ... Utrubique/Utrubi with quotations from Naevius, Cato, Plautus and Ulpian, running on into 'huiusce')
verdict.evidence: 'Our friend Caninius advised me in your words' and the Explanatio note on 'Utrubi ... in the Tarentilla, according to Carisius' are both printed on page 454. The only additions are short glosses such as <note>Caesar</note>. The English stops partway through 'The same man recites these word', so the page's last few lines (the Cato, Plautus and Ulpian quotations) are left out.

verdict.printed: Pages 856–857: the end of the introduction to Art. IV (Dionysius, Athenagoras, Ambrose), the ASSERTIO, §76 against Bañez with a long side column on his change of opinion, the column-2 text continuing onto 857, the heading 'Diuina libertas non potest exponi per solam indifferentiam obiectiuam', and §77.
verdict.evidence: 'He wrote this corollary in the second conclusion of that tenth article... through the new Sun of this doctrine' renders the first column of 857 on page -445. The English then stops at '857 And to omit the rest, this very diffi', so the second column of 857 (the heading and §77) is missing. The only additions are short glosses and notes, such as 'Domingo Bañez, a prominent Dominican theologian'.

verdict.printed: Page 206 (fol. 69, LIB. IIII) holds the end of Gellius's discussion of '-osus' words (vinosus, ingeniosus, facundiosa, and others), the heading of Chapter X on the order of asking senators' opinions, and its first sentence, which breaks off at 'qui a CENS.'
verdict.evidence: The English renders all of page 206 but then keeps going into page 207: 'he who had been chosen as prince by the Censors... Gaius Caesar, in the consulship which he held with Marcus Bibulus... ordered Cato to be released' and 'What and of what kind are those things which Aristoxenus...' are all printed on page 207.
